specification.outcome: During a long readiness operation invoked by tiber_workflow_request, Pi renders prompt activity within 100 ms, keeps animating, and replaces progress with one deterministic terminal result.

scenarios.name: yield and report bounded progress
given: executeEntry is monotonic time captured as the first execute statement
a test-controlled readiness promise remains pending for two seconds
then: running onUpdate is called before dispatch and no later than executeEntry plus 100 ms
a setImmediate sentinel scheduled after execute returns its promise runs before the readiness promise is resolved
later changed progress and unchanged heartbeats obey the anchored cadence

scenarios.name: apply one progress cadence
given: t0 is the successful initial-update time and normalized observation text is safe bounded text
then: each half-open interval [t0+n*1000,t0+(n+1)*1000) permits at most one changed update, with a 50 ms scheduler tolerance and skipped rather than replayed missed intervals
an unchanged heartbeat is due at t0+2000*k plus up to 50 ms
a changed update due at the same boundary replaces the heartbeat and no running-update gap exceeds 2050 ms

scenarios.name: select and render one terminal result
given: dispatch returns a typed success or denial or observes failure, abort, or deadline
when: the microtask arbitration checkpoint immediately before return observes available causes
then: precedence is caller abort, operation deadline, onUpdate failure, dispatch failure, typed denial, success
abort or deadline observed after dispatch settles but before commit wins; signals after commit are ignored
running updates stop and the host renderer replaces them from the execute return value

scenarios.name: cancel readiness and guard consequential effects
given: the 60000 ms operation deadline starts at executeEntry and includes setup and dispatch
readiness uses the Pi session AbortSignal contract and must acknowledge abort within 1000 ms
then: the linked signal aborts the reviewer session and cleanup is awaited through executeEntry plus 61000 ms
failure to acknowledge invokes session disposal and returns failed rather than leaving an owned session active
signal checks immediately before signed specification, Ready, claim, and worktree effects deny any effect after cancellation observation

scenarios.name: clean up races and malformed callbacks
given: initial or later onUpdate may throw, timer setup may throw, callbacks may already be queued, or readiness may resolve or reject late
then: removable timers, listeners, subscriptions, and session resources are disposed
already queued callbacks compare their captured generation and become no-ops
initial onUpdate failure emits no running state, performs no dispatch, and returns failed

acceptanceCriteria: Pi schema rejection occurs before execute and emits no Tiber progress. Semantic denial inside dispatch receives initial progress then a denied return. Initial update occurs before any synchronous dispatch setup; if monotonic measurement nonetheless exceeds 100 ms, dispatch is skipped and failed is returned.

Running update payload is {content:[{type:'text',text:<safe text>}],details:{disposition:'reviewing',sequence:<positive integer>,kind:'progress'|'heartbeat'}}. A change means normalized text differs from the last emitted text. Text rejects controls and is capped at 4096 characters.

Spinner animation remains Pi-owned and independent; Tiber preserves one tool-call identity and does not represent percentage completion. Heartbeats communicate only that the same operation is pending.

Dispatch returns a typed union. Success maps to details.disposition evaluated and sanitized host text; TiberFailure maps to denied and 'CODE: safe message'; caller abort maps to cancelled/TIBER_WORKFLOW_REQUEST_CANCELLED; the 60000 ms deadline maps to timed-out/TIBER_WORKFLOW_REQUEST_TIMED_OUT; callback, setup, malformed payload, or infrastructure defects map to failed/TIBER_WORKFLOW_REQUEST_EXECUTION_FAILED.

At the pre-return microtask checkpoint simultaneous cause precedence is cancelled, timed-out, failed-onUpdate, failed-dispatch, denied, evaluated. Exactly one terminal ToolResult is returned; onUpdate never carries terminal state.

The cancellable long-operation capability for this task is specifically Pi readiness session prompt plus session.abort/session.dispose. Synchronous signed publication and worktree effects are not started after signal observation and are covered for general responsiveness by the separate submitted-message ticket.
All removable resources are disposed and queued callbacks are generation-guarded. Existing workflow and authority decisions remain unchanged.
exclusions: Changing readiness findings or workflow authority
dependencies: Pi extension ToolResult, onUpdate, and AbortSignal contract
Pi readiness AgentSession prompt, abort, and dispose contract
pre-effect signal checks for specification, Ready, claim, and worktree effects
specification.architectureImplications: Add a closed progress/cancellation state machine around asynchronous readiness dispatch. Progress is bounded UI observation, terminal arbitration is deterministic, Pi session work is abortable and owned, and cancellation is rechecked before consequential workflow effects.
